text: Cytoplasm [Gr. kutoV , hollow, + plasma , anything formed]: Ger. Zellkörper ; Fr. cytoplasme ; Ital. citoplasma . The protoplasmic substance of the cell-body as contrasted with that of the nucleus (karyoplasm). A term proposed by Strasburger in 1882. See E. B. Wilson, The Cell in Devel . and Inheritance , 1896. ( C.LL.M. )
